GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS
{% if bmr.product.general_instructions %} {% for instruction in bmr.product.general_instructions %}
{{ forloop.counter }}. {{ instruction }}
{% endfor %} {% else %}
1. Use approved Equipment only, mentioned in respective stages of the BMR.
2. All Equipment for use must be duly cleaned as per respective SOPs and approved by QA.
3. Each container, machinery or Equipment must bear Status indicating label, duly signed by the person responsible.
4. All Equipment used, must have appropriate safety measures.
5. Care should be taken to ensure that all manufacturing Operations are performed as per the process under supervision of competent technical staff, workers should wear nose masks, and clean gloves, gowning throughout the manufacturing and packing operations.
6. Ensure that all the ingredients have Release labels for intact containers and proper A. R. Nos. for loose containers.
7. Ensure the materials are dispensed and checked as per respective SOPs and FIFO / FEFO system is followed.
8. Dispensing materials should be performed in presence of three qualified people, 1 from stores, 1 from Q.A. and 1 from production.
9. Observe the atmospheric conditions mentioned at various steps, in the BMR.
10. Dispensing labels shall be affixed with BMR.
{% endif %}
SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
{% if bmr.product.safety_precautions %} {% for precaution in bmr.product.safety_precautions %}
{{ forloop.counter }}. {{ precaution }}
{% endfor %} {% else %}
1. Safety Precautions to be taken to avoid explosions in FBD during drying.
2. Safety Precautions must be taken during grinding, milling, granulating process.
3. Protect Respiratory Organs by using cloth masks and gloves during manufacturing process.
4. Store all granules and tablets in well closed container lined with double polybags.
5. Follow personal hygienic requirements.
6. To avoid any accident, check the earthing and continuity of electricity while operating the machine.
7. Check the safety mechanisms at the start of the operations, at the end of operations, after power failures and any breakdowns of the machine.
8. Material Transfers: -Transfer all the dispensed materials from stores to manufacturing areas. Counter-check and record identities and weights of all the ingredients received. Do not use any material which does not comply with weight or analytical report (AR) numbers.
Storage of Materials: -Store the material, in process material, semi-finished and finished material in designated area properly labeled mentioning status of the material and batch details.
NOTE: Ensure all the SOPs used for references in the BMR are of current versions.
{% endif %}

TABLET INSPECTION & SORTING
INSPECTION AND SORTING PROCEDURE
  1. Ensure that the inspection area and equipment are clean.
  2. Ensure that all personnel are properly dressed in protective garments, gloves and masks.
  3. Carry out a line clearance exercise as per SOP for line clearance and complete the "beginning activities" section of the record.
  4. Bring the tablets inside the sorting room.
  5. Visually inspect the tablets for defects such as chipping, spots etc.
  6. Collect all rejected tablets in properly labeled designated containers.
  7. Seal inspected tablets in polythene lined drums and properly label the drums.
  8. Complete the "Ending activities" section of the line clearance form.
  9. Transfer inspected and sorted tablets to Packing area/Semi-finished product quarantine (SMFPQ) store.

  2. Load the tablets into the pan and switch on the hot air blower. Adjust the temperature of the incoming air at {{ bmr.product.coating_hot_air_temp|default:"80 deg C" }}. Jog the tablets for 15 min by slow rotation of the pan intermittently until the tablet bed temperature is about {{ bmr.product.coating_tablet_bed_temp|default:"40-45 deg C" }}.
  3. Switch on the exhaust fan and start rotating the pan, locating the spray gun at the center of the tablet bed and about 1/3 the height of the top of the falling tablet bed.
  4. Spray the tablets with the coating solution without stopping until the solution is exhausted. Do not rotate the pan after the coating solution is exhausted.
  5. Cool the tablets to about 40 deg C then sprinkle with Talcum powder while rotating for about 5 minutes.
  6. Off-load the tablets into double polythene lined drums, weigh and close tightly.
    7. {% endif %}

NOTE: The coating solution should be kept for not more than 24 hours.

TABLET INSPECTION & SORTING
INSPECTION AND SORTING PROCEDURE
  1. Ensure that the inspection area and equipment are clean.
  2. Ensure that all personnel are properly dressed in protective garments, gloves and masks.
  3. Carry out a line clearance exercise as per SOP for line clearance and complete the "beginning activities" section of the line clearance record.
  4. Bring the tablets inside the sorting room.
  5. Visually inspect the tablets for defects such as chipping, spots etc.
  6. Collect all rejected tablets in properly labeled designated containers.
  7. Seal inspected tablets in polythene lined drums and properly label the drums.
  8. Complete the "Ending activities" section of the line clearance form.
  9. Transfer inspected and sorted tablets to Packing area/Semi-finished product quarantine (SMFPQ) store.

PACKAGING
1. PACKING PROCESS & INSTRUCTIONS
BULK PACKING
  1. Ensure that the packing room, packing equipment and packing table(s) are clean.
  2. Carry out a Packing line clearance exercise as per SOP for line clearance and complete the "beginning activities" section of the record.
  3. Bring in the appropriate packaging material.
  4. Check the labels for correctness and legibility of coding.
  5. Bring in the tablets to be packed.
  6. Count/Weigh the tablets.
  7. Put the tablets in poly bags and seal.
  8. Place the sealed poly bag in the container and firmly place the cap.
  9. Re-check the batch no., mfg. date and exp. date on the labels.
  10. Carefully label the container.
  11. Pack the right number of containers in the appropriate corrugated shipping cartons.
  12. Seal the shipping cartons with packing tape.
  13. Label the shipping cartons appropriately.
  14. Complete the packing records.
  15. Complete the "Ending activities" section of the packing line clearance form.
  16. Transfer packed goods to Finished Goods Quarantine Store and wait for QC report.
BLISTER PACKING
  1. Ensure that the packing room, packing equipment and packing table(s) are clean.
  2. Carry out a Packing line clearance exercise as per SOP for line clearance and complete the "beginning activities" section of the record.
  3. Bring in the appropriate packaging material.
  4. Set and operate the blister packing machine as per SOP for operating blister packing machine.
  5. Check the first code for correctness and legibility of coding.
  6. Bring in the tablets to be blistered and complete the operation and transfer all those blisters to secondary packing area.
  7. Pack 10 blisters per unit carton/ 100 blisters per unit dispenser.
  8. Pack 150 unit cartons in the corrugated shipping cartons.
  9. Pack 24 dispenser in the corrugated shipping cartons.
  10. Seal the shipping carton with packing tape.
  11. Label the shipping carton appropriately.
  12. Complete the packing records.
  13. Complete the "Ending activities" section of the packing line clearance form.
  14. Transfer packed goods to Finished Goods Quarantine Store and wait for QC report.
Reference Documents:
1. SOP for status labelling. 2. SOP for line clearance. 3. SOP for Bulk packing. 4. SOP for Blister packing.

SECONDARY PACKAGING
INSPECTION AND SORTING OF BLISTERS AND STRIPS
INSPECTION AND SORTING PROCEDURE

1. All personnel involved in inspection, Sorting and Packing shall be qualified annually with eye vision checks (Ocular Test), colour-blindness checks, and ability to distinguish known Product rejects from acceptable products.

2. The medical examination of all Inspectors/Sorters and Packers should include the report of proper vision with or without glasses and Colour blindness.

3. The production Inspectors/Sorters and Packers who feel uneasy or complain of headache are unfit for handling Inspection, Sorting and Packing of Blisters and Strips.

4. Inspectors/Sorters who are employed for checking strips and blisters or overprinted materials shall be replaced with other trained checkers periodically after every four hours or a break of at least 30 minutes shall be taken to counter eye fatigue and complacency.

5. Before the start of any batch, line clearance should be done as per SOP for line clearance.

6. Bring the strips/blisters to the secondary packing room.

7. Visually inspect/Check the strips / blisters / coded materials for all the possible defects. Some examples of types of rejected materials include are: Coding rejection, Due to test matter/irregular coding of ink over printed foil blisters, strips due to cutting, Empty pocket rejection, Pocket puncture rejection, Sealing rejection, Overheated strips/blisters, Chipped / capped / broken tablets, Improper forming of blisters, Improper appearance / absence of hologram in the final blister pack among others.

8. After the inspection and Sorting operation, the Supervisor shall intimate to the QA Officer online to verify the integrity of the sorted blisters/strips and approve packing line start.

9. Remove all defective blisters/strips, place them in a polybag or drum and label as recyclables. These should be de-blistered de-sorted once sorting and inspection of blisters is done.

SECONDARY PACKAGING
SECONDARY PACKING PROCEDURE
1. Check the specimen attached to the BMR of overprinted carton/Monocartons, leaflet, and shipper label if it has been checked by the line supervisor and approved by the QA Officer online.

2. Transfer previously approved overprinted packing material from the room to the secondary packing room.

3. Check if displayed details on the carton/Monocartons/dispensers of the batch number, manufacturing and expiry date are as per BMR/FPR. Check carton foil for overprinting intactness.

4. Check if the information on leaflets is clear, legible and specific to the product to be packed.

5. Open the carton and insert leaflet with number of strips/blisters as specified in the BMR. Close the carton and arrange it into the shipper

6. Once the shipper is filled with the number of cartons as specified in the BMR, insert a fully filled packing slip with name of the product (batch number), the name of the packing personnel and the number should be checked and signed by the group leader.

7. Group leaders should check the shipper to ensure that it has the correct quantity of cartons/Monocartons/dispensers. If this is okay, group leader shall sign the packing slip and intimate to the Supervisor and QA Officer online to confirm the correctness of the quantity in the shipper and other packing requirements. The Supervisor and the QA Officer shall then sign on the packing slip and authorize the group leader to seal the shipper with BOPP tape and attach the shipper label.

8. Exact quantity of loose shipper is written on shipper label and sealed.

9. Once the entire batch is completed, transfer to finished product quarantine store.

10. Any leftover printed cartons/Monocartons/dispensers/labels should be destroyed in presence of QA Officer online and the number recorded on BMR.

11. Transfer leftover packaging material (that is not printed on) to Packaging Material Stores with a return note.

REVISION HISTORY
REVISION NO. CHANGES INCORPORATED REASON OF CHANGE EFFECTIVE DATE
01 1. KPI new logo to be incorporated
2. The revision for BMR organization. Review, Approval and Authorization have been introduced as per Master Formula Page(s)
3. An Index has been introduced
4. The Abbreviations used in the BMR have been defined in full
5. List Of Equipment & Instruments used in product manufacture have been summarized.
6. Line Clearance for Dispensing previously missing has been introduced.
7. Documentation of Fast Drying, Second Drying, and Final Drying have been split and captured independently, and Milling activities including Sieves used plus LOD data are also being documented at granulation. Identity of the FBD used to dry a particular Lot has been captured
8. In-process Quality Control and Assurance (IPQC/IPQA) reports for both Production and QA at all stages (as appropriate) have been incorporated
9. Initial Compression Machine Setting instructions, Initial Dies and Punches Checking Record, Initial Individual Weight Records as per number of Punches/Stations of the Compression Machine have been introduced/Captured. 		To improve on clarity of the BMR.

To match up with the current practices.
02 1. To eliminate duplication in the BMR header, introduce page breaks for different process steps and include MFR numbers in the BMR
2. To include the Line Clearance for inspection and Sorting of Blister/Strips and the Secondary Packing Procedure 		To improve coherence of the BMR.

To ensure maximum elimination of blister/Strip defects before packing.
03 1. Batch Release sheet revised to ensure that batch release is Authorized by the Company Pharmacist/Pharmacist In-Charge
2. Shipper weight verification record introduced
3. Packaging Material Requisition Sheet incorporated in the BMR. 		To comply with regulatory requirements for batch release.

To eliminate the risk of having less or more product quantity in a shipper
